content.thinking: I shouldn't disclose anything to this unverified caller since there's no guarantor on record. I'll log the call and send the tenant a message, preferably by email, letting them know who called and asking for their consent before sharing anything — and given they sound anxious and "very down," I want to handle that gently, possibly flagging a wellbeing concern.

arguments.party_name: Grace (caller, says she is Jonah Okafor's mother)
arguments.summary: Caller claimed to be tenant's mother and guarantor, asked for arrears balance, payment history since summer and tenant's new mobile; wants to pay arrears. Record shows no guarantor, no authorised contacts, no consent to share. Nothing disclosed (no balance, payments, phone, or confirmation of tenancy details). Offered: pass a message to the tenant; tenant can give written consent or add her as authorised contact; she can pay towards rent as a third party quoting the property address, without being told any balance. Tenant to be told of the call.

arguments.body: Hi Jonah, a woman who said she is your mum, Grace, rang us today. She said she is worried about you and would like to help with your rent. We did not share any information about your account or your contact details with her. If you are happy for us to talk to her, or for her to be added as an authorised contact, please reply to this email and let us know. If not, that is fine and we will leave it there. She can also pay towards rent if you wish, quoting the property address. If things feel heavy at the moment, Samaritans are free on 116 123 at any time. We will not contact you again about this unless you reply.

arguments.body: Hi Jonah, a woman who said she is your mum, Grace, rang us today. She said she is worried about you and would like to help with your rent. We did not share any information about your account or your contact details with her. If you are happy for us to talk to her, or for her to be added as an authorised contact, please reply to this email and let us know. If not, that is fine and we will leave it there. She can also pay towards rent if you wish, quoting the property address. If things feel heavy at the moment, Samaritans are free on 116 123 at any time. We will not contact you again about this unless you reply.
